I think the distribution of the votes and the default bin width is
messing things up (likely needs better failure handling). You could
mess about with small bin widths, but I think what you really want to do
is scale the data rather than the coordinates.

m + geom_histogram() + scale_x_log10()

or

m <- ggplot(movies, aes(x=log10(votes))) + geom_histogram()

Hello Mark,

Thank you for your reply.

Mark Connolly <mark_c...@acm.org> writes:

> I think the distribution of the votes and the default bin width is
> messing things up (likely needs better failure handling). You could
> mess about with small bin widths, but I think what you really want to
> do is scale the data rather than the coordinates.
>
> m + geom_histogram() + scale_x_log10()
>

I have just read the ggplot2 Springer UseR! book. I am aware that I need
to transform _after_ statistics, for I want a stack-positioned histogram
(so I need coord_trans(y="log"), I was experimenting with x though).

Now the problem is solved. It is because the axis range before
transformation is [0, xx) so log gives [-Inf, log(xx)), for which
ggplot2 did not have a mechanism (at least a clear error message to
point it out) to handle. After some search, I have found
coord_trans(y="log1p") is the right thing to use, it applies log(x+1)
instead of log(x); therefore no -Inf issue.

One quick question: how can I define a custimized coord_trans function?
e.g. log10(x+1)?

Just for the search engine records:
the problem with the coordinates transformation log10 is described in
http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_histogram.html
But as you said, the error given could be a bit more informative.
Also is important to notice that the scale transformation applies to
the transformed data but the coordinate transformation to the raw
data.

-- <code from http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/geom_histogram.html>--
m <- ggplot(movies, aes(x = votes))
> # For __transformed scales__, **binwidth applies to the transformed data**.
> # The bins have constant width on the transformed scale.

# For __transformed coordinate systems__, the **binwidth applies to the
# raw data**. The bins have constant width on the original scale.

# Using **log scales does not work here**, because the first
# bar is anchored at zero, and so when transformed becomes negative
# infinity. This is not a problem when transforming the scales, because
# no observations have 0 ratings.
m + geom_histogram() + coord_trans(x = "log10")
## [error] no output
--<end code>---
